text: A representation of a group $G$ over a field $k$ is, by definition:
choices: a group homomorphism $\rho:G\to GL(V)$ for a $k$-vector space $V$
explanation: A representation is a group homomorphism $\rho:G\to GL(V)$ sending each $g$ to an invertible linear map. The equivalent ring-homomorphism packaging is $k[G]\to\mathrm{End}_k(V)$ (from the group algebra, not from $G$ itself); a bare $k$-linear map forgets the group action; and demanding an isomorphism is too strong, since many representations (e.g. the trivial one) are far from injective.
